newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippines Petron confirms first gas oil export.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Petron confirms first gas oil export.

text.p: Philippines' Petron Corp on Tuesday confirmed its first spot gas oil export which was sealed on Friday and would consider more exports if there were surplus volumes and international prices remained high.
The 17,000-to-18,000-tonne parcel of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil was sold around $29.00 per barrel for October 12-15 lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Bataan, Petron sources said.
Trade sources said the cargo might be delivered to China.
"There was a negotiated export," one source said. "It's a one-off sale and is not a regular export."

Another source said, "This is just a spot cargo and we are not planning to export on a regular basis. We usually look at the domestic market, but if there are extra volumes and the price is good we may export more."
Petron raised the capacity of its Bataan refinery to 165,000 barrels per day from 155,000 bpd last December. This enabled it to hike gas oil output to 40,000-45,000 bpd from over 30,000 bpd.
Physical gas oil rallied to a five-year on October 2 when a deal was traded at $29.70 a barrel fob Singapore. It has remained high since then and was bid at $29.75 on Monday.
